items.title: Diet Coke, beer makers get 6-month breather as govt extends aluminium can certification deadline
items.summary: The government has extended the deadline for quality certification of aluminium beverage cans to April 2027. The extension provides manufacturers necessary time to increase production amidst growing demand. Many brands are experiencing supply challenges due to disruptions from the Middle East conflict. The beverage industry had hoped to produce additional cans but fell short of expectations. Consequently, manufacturers are seeking regulatory relief as they attempt to meet rising consumer needs.

items.title: Tata Motors CV posts Rs 2,138 crore Q2 profit
items.summary: Tata Motors Ltd achieved a standalone net profit of ₹2,138 crore for the September quarter, reversing last year's loss. Revenue from operations rose significantly to ₹23,930 crore, up 42% from the previous year. Improved demand was driven by higher fleet utilization and industrial activity, according to managing director Girish Wagh. Consolidated profit also increased to ₹1,257 crore, aided by a drop in mark-to-market losses.

items.title: Lava MD Sunil Raina, CFO Rajesh Sethi exit amid turnaround

items.title: Commerce minister Piyush Goyal discusses investment avenues with German companies
items.summary: Piyush Goyal engaged with major German firms like Siemens Healthineers, Bayer, and Fresenius to discuss investments. He highlighted Bayer's plans for expansion and collaboration in India's healthcare ecosystem. Goyal also addressed opportunities for Fresenius to leverage India's talent for healthcare solutions. Furthermore, he explored ways to strengthen Siemens Healthineers' presence in the country. These discussions reflect India's growing relevance in the global healthcare market.

items.title: Private sector activity hits four month high in October
items.summary: India's private sector activity experienced significant growth in October, reaching a four-month high as new orders increased. The HSBC Flash India Composite Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 56.7, signaling expansion. Manufacturing output and new orders remained stable, while services activity saw notable improvement. Employment increased slightly, although firms showed caution in hiring due to adequate staffing levels. International demand contributed to growth, with export orders expanding significantly during this period.

items.title: Link fertiliser subsidies to area & crop productivity: ICRIER
items.summary: India is recommended to shift from product-based fertiliser subsidies to direct support for farmers to improve soil health. It involves integrating digital records of cultivation and crop-specific nutrient requirements for more effective subsidy targeting. The reports emphasize the necessity of incorporating tenant farmers and sharecroppers in these digital systems. Improved targeting of subsidies could lead to better investment in soil health and sustainable practices.

items.title: DGCA extends pilot rest rule deadline to March as airlines face cost pressures
items.summary: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation has extended the deadline for revised pilot rest rules to March 31, 2027. This extension is a response to airlines facing challenges such as rising costs and crew availability issues. Previous relaxations were granted after major operational disruptions by IndiGo due to crew shortages. Airline associations argue that these extensions undermine safety regulations and hinder compliance.

items.title: Airlines oppose any cuts in slots at Mumbai airport

They demand data on airport capacity and Terminal 1 redevelopment details before changes are made. The Airport Operators Committee insists compliance with existing guidelines and clear justifications for any slot changes. Terminal 1 is currently handling under 10 million passengers per annum, while capacity at Terminal 2 is expected to increase.
